target_customer: Licensed cannabis dispensaries and delivery operators
problem: Legal cannabis retailers need point of sale, online ordering, delivery and state compliance reporting in one system.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for dispensary POS, ecommerce, delivery and compliance

founders.name: David Hua
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a co-founder and advocate for progressive cannabis. A search summary says the idea came while attending Oaksterdam University in February 2014, not verified on an opened page.

founders.name: Rick Harrison
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder and CTO.

founders.name: Scott A Garman
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background.

founders.name: Harrison Lee
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as designer and developer.

technical_complexity.rationale: Starting as a delivery and order platform then adding POS, inventory and state seed to sale compliance (Metrc) integrations required standard engineering with regulatory complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Compliance integrations and embedded POS data make dispensaries slow to switch, but several POS vendors compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large acquirer emerged; many cannabis POS rivals (Dutchie, Treez, Flowhub, Cova per current listings) grew later while Meadow stayed independent.

market_need_then: California medical marijuana dispensaries lacked modern software; TechCrunch covered Meadow's 2014 launch as an 'Uber for weed' and YC noted it as its first cannabis startup.

branding.name_origin: CEO David Hua has said the name came from his time at Oaksterdam and was chosen to evoke gathering, calm, healing and sanctuary.
branding.domain_note: Uses getmeadow.com, a prefix domain; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Simple, intuitive, all in one and compliance focused.

branding.community_and_virality: A cannabis industry outlet carried an interview with Hua on branding; the company claims the top cannabis POS rating on G2 (self reported).

brand_strength.rationale: Calm, memorable name suited to the category and strong B2B reputation claims, but no evidence of consumer brand pull.

pivots.from: Marijuana delivery and order management platform
pivots.to: Dispensary point of sale and inventory software
pivots.why: Seed announcement said the money would expand the platform with a POS and inventory tool

outcome_analysis: Meadow started with cannabis delivery in 2014, raised a 2.1M seed in 2016 and moved into dispensary POS and compliance software as state markets legalized. It expanded to Michigan in 2022 and several more states and is still active with about 14 staff. Later funding is not verified, so growth is shown mainly by its customer list and expansion news.
notes: Seed confirmed by the company blog, VentureBeat, MJBizDaily and TechCrunch; a Chronicle article put total funding at 2.2M. Aggregators list later rounds under 'Meadow Care' (2019, 2021) that may be a different entity, unverified. No 2015 era competitor source found; G2 lists are current and omitted. No outcome news found. The first seed announcement said it was raised on a rolling basis over about a year after YC.
